title: Jesus did not give His harshest warning to atheists.
paragraphs:
Jesus did not give His harshest warning to atheists.
He did not give it to pagans.
He did not give it to corrupt governments.
He gave it to a church.

Not a persecuted church.
Not a struggling church.
A comfortable church.
And His words were chilling.

“I know your works, that you are neither cold nor hot. I wish you were either one or the other. So, because you are lukewarm—neither hot nor cold—I will spit you out of My mouth.”
— Revelation 3:15–16
This is one of the most unsettling warnings Jesus ever spoke.
Because it wasn’t directed at the world.
It was directed at people who thought they were doing fine spiritually.
The Danger of Lukewarm Faith
The lukewarm church isn’t rebellious.
It’s comfortable.

It attends services.
It sings the songs.
It knows the language of faith.
But something is missing.
There is no fire.

No deep hunger for God.
No burning love for truth.
No urgency for repentance.
No trembling reverence for the presence of Christ.
Just routine.
Just religion.
Just spiritual temperature neutrality.
And according to Jesus, that state is dangerous.
Because lukewarm faith feels safe while slowly drifting away from the heart of God.
Why Lukewarm Christianity Is So Deceptive
Cold hearts often know they are far from God.
But lukewarm hearts believe they are close enough.
They assume:

“I go to church.”
“I believe in God.”
“I’m not a bad person.”
“I’m better than most.”
But Jesus sees deeper than appearances.
He sees the condition of the heart.
And in Revelation 3, He reveals the problem.
The church believed it was spiritually rich.
But Jesus said something shocking:

“You say, ‘I am rich; I have acquired wealth and do not need a thing.’
But you do not realize that you are wretched, pitiful, poor, blind and naked.”
— Revelation 3:17
Imagine hearing those words from Christ.
They thought they were thriving spiritually.
But in heaven’s perspective, they were spiritually empty.
The Modern Church Should Pay Attention
This warning was written almost 2,000 years ago.
But it may describe many churches today.
Church buildings grow bigger.
Technology improves.
Music becomes more polished.
But sometimes the one thing that fades is the most important:
Holy fire.
Faith becomes culture instead of conviction.
Christianity becomes identity instead of surrender.
We begin to follow a comfortable Jesus instead of the living King who calls us to repentance and transformation.
And slowly, subtly, the flame cools.
Until what remains is lukewarm faith.
Jesus’ Words Were Not Just a Warning — They Were a Wake-Up Call
Many people focus on the warning.
But they miss the invitation.
Because Jesus did not abandon the lukewarm church.
He called them to return.
Just a few verses later, He says:

“Those whom I love I rebuke and discipline. So be earnest and repent.”
— Revelation 3:19
That sentence reveals something powerful.
The warning comes from love.
Jesus confronts lukewarmness because He cares about His church.
He refuses to let people drift toward spiritual death without sounding the alarm.
The rebuke is not rejection.
It is mercy.
The Invitation Is Still Open
One of the most famous verses in Revelation follows this warning.

“Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in and eat with that person, and they with me.”
— Revelation 3:20
Think about that.
Jesus was speaking to a church.
Yet He described Himself as standing outside the door.
Knocking.
Waiting.
Inviting.
Not forcing.
Not condemning.
But calling.
Calling hearts back to real relationship with Him.
The Question That Matters
This message is not just about ancient churches.
It’s about us.
Every believer.
Every congregation.
Every heart.
The real question is not:
“Do I attend church?”
The real question is:
Is my heart on fire for Christ?
Do we hunger for truth?
Do we love His presence?
Do we repent when convicted?
Do we seek Him when no one is watching?
Or have we become spiritually comfortable?
Lukewarm Faith Is Easy.
But True Faith Burns.
True faith costs something.
It requires surrender.
It requires humility.
It requires choosing obedience even when it is unpopular.
But it also brings something the lukewarm life never can:
Real life.
Real joy.
Real peace.
Real transformation.
The fire of God is not meant to destroy us.
It is meant to refine us.
A Watchman’s Reminder
This warning is not meant to shame anyone.
It is meant to wake us up.
Because as long as there is breath in our lungs, the invitation remains open.
The door can still be opened.
The fire can still be rekindled.
And Jesus is still calling hearts back to Him.
🔥 So here’s the honest question:
Do you think the modern church struggles with lukewarm faith today?
Or do you believe this warning only applied to the early church?
